commitResults.messageTitle: Add task types and console UI testing workflow
Add exception handling and expanded UI edge-case tests
Add date and time parsing for deadlines and events
Fix UI test expectations and final console formatting
Add help and clear task commands

commitResults.messageBody: Move Nob's welcome, farewell, divider, help, and command-hint output into a dedicated Ui class. This establishes a small presentation boundary while preserving command processing, task storage, and all existing console behavior.

Move task-file loading, task-record decoding, and task-file writing from Nob into Storage. Nob now coordinates Storage and Ui while retaining the current task array, command handling, and user-visible behavior for this incremental refactor.

Move task storage, capacity checks, list mutation, and task-number validation from Nob into TaskList. Nob now coordinates commands, persistence, and user-facing responses while TaskList owns the mutable task collection.

Move task-command syntax validation, task construction, and task-number conversion from Nob into Parser. Nob now delegates argument interpretation while continuing to coordinate command routing, task-list updates, persistence, and presentation.

Move task-list display, task mutation responses, capacity feedback, and user-facing error messages from Nob into Ui. Nob now coordinates command handling, parsing, task updates, and persistence without formatting task-related console output.

Add the Command abstraction and move Nob's farewell behavior into ExitCommand. This establishes the command-pattern execution contract while preserving the existing loop and leaving other command branches for later incremental extraction.
Move Nob's help response into a HelpCommand that implements the shared Command execution contract. This extends the command pattern with a non-mutating command while preserving console behavior.
Move Nob's list response into ListCommand, extending the shared Command execution pattern to a read-only task command while preserving output.
Move task clearing, persistence, and completion feedback from Nob into ClearCommand. This establishes the shared command pattern for a state-changing operation while preserving existing behavior.
Place application, command, task, UI, storage, parser, exception, and utility classes in responsibility-based nob packages. Update UI test launch commands for the packaged entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for core Nob logic

commitResults.messageBody:
Javadoc tags and several production lines do not fully follow the Java coding standard.

Standardize tag punctuation and wrap long lines to improve consistency and readability without changing application behavior.

Java changes need consistent, project-specific guidance to meet the SE-EDU intermediate standard.

Add a reusable coding-standard skill and require it for production and JUnit changes so future updates follow the same conventions.

Future commits need consistent messages and focused staging to keep history understandable.

Add an SE-EDU Git conventions skill and require it before creating project commits.

Users cannot locate tasks by their descriptions when the list grows.

Add a case-insensitive find command, display matching tasks with their original numbers, and cover the behavior in unit and console UI tests.

Nob currently runs only through a terminal, which limits the Level-10 user experience. Add an FXML-based chat window with custom avatars, persistent task commands, and a minimal visual theme. Retain the console runner and its regression plan so existing behavior remains verifiable.

Several exit and date-time helper methods have no callers in the console or JavaFX applications. Remove those APIs and the empty duplicate exception file to keep the project surface small and easier to maintain.

The Checkstyle plugin is enabled but its configuration is missing, causing the standard verification task to fail before checking code. Restore the project SE-EDU rules and align existing test imports and wrapping so the complete Gradle check succeeds.

Parser, storage, task-list and FXML code relyy on assumptions that may be
easy to violate during future changes.

Add assertions to detect invalid commands, task-list state, task data and
missing FXML resources early during development.

Kept invalid user input handled through exception handling.

Nob.main handles setup, input reading, command dispatch, and error
reporting in one long method. These mixed responsibilities obscure the
application control flow and make command changes harder to review.

Extract command dispatch and invalid-command handling into small helper
methods. This keeps the main loop at one level of abstraction while
preserving the existing console behavior.
Add assertions

Storage.parseTask handles validation, task-type detection, field
parsing, and completion restoration in one method. Repeated format
literals also make the storage contract difficult to identify and update
safely.

Extract format constants and type-specific parsing helpers. This keeps
each method at one level of abstraction and gives every part of the
saved-task format a clear name.

MainWindow.executeCommand handles top-level commands and every task
operation in one long conditional chain. This makes the main dispatch
flow harder to scan and extend.

Extract task-specific dispatch and use early returns for top-level
commands. This keeps the happy path flat and each method focused on one
level of abstraction without changing chatbot responses.

Parser repeats command names, delimiters, and usage text throughout its
validation logic. These magic literals hide the command grammar and make
future syntax changes prone to inconsistent updates.

Give each syntax element and reusable message a descriptive constant.
This makes parsing calculations self-explanatory and keeps repeated
guidance consistent while preserving all existing responses.
Branch a code quality

Task serialization currently uses a manual loop and mutable builder even
though every task undergoes the same conversion. This adds bookkeeping
that obscures the transformation being performed.

Use an array stream to convert and join the active tasks. This expresses
the serialization as a direct data pipeline while preserving the saved
file format.
Use streams to serialize tasks

The assertion, code-quality, and Streams merges leave duplicate task
serialization code and reintroduce raw command literals. As a result,
master does not compile and no longer consistently uses its named
format helpers.

Remove the stale serialization loop, validate preconditions before using
the task array, and reuse the parser and storage constants. This restores
the reviewed structure while retaining assertions and stream-based
serialization.
